rv.q: He carries the show with an unbridled, infectious, childlike enthusiasm, sharing what he knows and loves–science and music–using songs he wrote in his car and lyrics that support his storytelling.
At its best, Emergence is a balm for what divides us with a sense of cosmic connection.
Defying logic, it all somehow works.
But the text is too self-consciously mystical and the songs all sound alike thanks to their droning melodies and elliptical lyrics.
Emergence is a genuinely refreshing addition to the season.
This show is uplifting, insightful and definitely a unique theatrical experience.
If you’re looking for a musical sermon about life, consciousness, perception, and the universe, Emergence offers the gospel truth.

If you are haunted by the questions “Are we alive?” How did we get here?” “What is the nature of time?” and “Where does human love originate?” and enjoy experimental works and immersive experiences with affirmative mind-expanding content, Emergence is one to consider.

I wanted the performative ideas and psychedelic elements to go farther–to readily, eagerly close my eyes when summoned and immerse myself into the experience; but the mesmerizing experience didn’t meet me.

cn.t: Critics are divided on Olson's ambitious multimedia fusion of science, music, and philosophy—some praise its originality and mind-expanding artistry, while others find it overly abstract and sermon-like despite captivating production elements.
